objective.text: The purpose of this grant was to conduct new simulations and ground-based experiments using ozone-sensitized counterflow flames to develop a new diagram of the flammability limits of diffusional cool flames affected by radiation, diffusion, and convection.
objective.quote: the purpose of this grant was to conduct new simulations and ground-based experiments using ozone-sensitized counterflow flames to: 1) Develop a new diagram of the flammability limits of diffusional cool flames affected by radiation, diffusion, and convection.

fuel.text: The fuel used in the study included n-heptane and dimethyl ether.
fuel.quote: spark-assisted flame propagation of a n-heptane/air mixture

sample_geometry.text: The geometry used involved a one-dimensional system.

pressure.text: Simulated cool flame regimes and burning limits were examined at elevated pressure up to 20 atm.
pressure.quote: simulated cool flame regimes and burning limits at elevated pressure (up to 20 atm) using DME/air mixtures.

variables.text: Factors such as oxygen concentration, dilution, pressure, diffusion, and convection transport processes affect the cool flame transition.
variables.quote: The investigation hypothesizes that factors such as oxygen concentration, dilution, pressure, diffusion, and convection transport processes affect the cool flame transition.

measurements.text: Measurements obtained include extinction limit, flame temperature, and species distribution.
measurements.quote: Obtain new, quantitative data of extinction limit, flame temperature, and species distribution for the validation of kinetic and radiation models involving cool flames.

earth_benefits.text: Cool flames and warm flames are relevant and important flame regimes for high-pressure near-limit combustion applications.
earth_benefits.quote: cool flames and warm flames are relevant and important flame regimes for high-pressure near-limit combustion applications.
